item.title: Like Bottom of the Hill, Thee Parkside Is Also Now Going to Close
item.description: "Well, looks like we’re gonna turn into a buncha condos," say the owners of Potrero Hill music venue Thee Parkside in an Instagram post featuring a video of graffiti being written saying "This Will Be Condos You Can't Afford."

item.title: San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan Declares He’s Running for Governor, Becomes Zillionth Democrat In the Race
item.description: Yet another Democratic candidate has declared for the 2026 California Governor’s race, and the tech industry now has their favorite guy in the mix, with three-year San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan throwing his hat in the ring.

item.title: Waymo Started Taking Passengers to SFO Today
item.description: Waymos are ferrying paying customers from SF to San Francisco International Airport for the first time on Thursday, but the robocars will not be able to take you directly to the terminals, at least not yet.

item.title: Peaches Christ to Host 30th Anniversary Screening of 'Showgirls' at Castro Theatre, With Star Gina Gershon
item.description: SF drag legend and midnight movie impresario Peaches Christ is returning home to the Castro Theatre as part of its grand reopening months, putting on a 30th anniversary screening of the cult classic "Showgirls."

item.title: Giant Holographic Schlong on Muni Is Actually an AI Ad, Muni Yanks It From Circulation
item.description: A real cock-up in the annals of Muni advertising, as users noted what appeared to be a holographic penis on the side of a bus, though it’s just an AI company ad that may have been approved willy-nilly.

item.title: Oakland's It's All Good Bakery Closes After 30 Years
item.description: Beloved Oakland bakery It's All Good, which opened inside the former Black Panthers headquarters in North Oakland in 1996, has permanently closed.

item.title: 7 Mile House Celebrates Its 168th Anniversary This Saturday, With $1.68 Jack Daniels Shots and More
item.description: Established in 1858, 7 Mile House at the SF-Brisbane border turns 168 years old on Saturday, and is celebrating with $1.68 Jack Daniels shots, free adobo, and a presentation on the restaurant's (often outlaw) 168-year history.

item.title: SF Bakery Selling Anti-ICE Cookies
item.description: Following recent violent events in Minneapolis, a San Francisco bakery is selling cookies with anti-ICE messages on them, alongside Valentine's cookies with traditional Valentine's heart candy abbreviations on them.

item.title: Mission Cultural Center Abruptly Closes, Was Apparently Drowning in Red Ink
item.description: Day of the Dead just won’t be the same without the Mission Cultural Center for Latino Arts, but the 47-year-old arts space gave up the ghost Monday, and is now desperately trying to get an advance to continue existing in some form.

item.title: Day Around the Bay: The Castro Theatre’s Long-Awaited New Organ Has Arrived
item.description: Super Bowl tickets are hitting the event’s second-highest price ever; a Waymo hit an elementary school student in SoCal; and the Castro Theatre's much-anticipated new digital organ has arrived and will soon make its debut.
